page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, delivering 2.0 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include a 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the multi-core capabilities of this instance in the top 25%, as demonstrated by strong results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and PassMark CPU physics testing. Memory performance is a notable strength, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, although large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain in the middle 50% average tier. Cryptographic operations perform well, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, which yield top 25% scores in PassMark CPU encryption. However, single-core performance and text processing tasks, such as Geekbench text processing and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the average category.

The instance demonstrates strong capabilities for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation via clang, and ray tracing, all scoring in the top 25%. It also shows top 10% performance in text generation for small LLM models, though prompt processing and larger model inference scale down to average speeds. Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the absence of local storage, and the strong multi-core and database benchmark results, this server is configured for database operations, multi-threaded backend services, and CPU-based rendering tasks that do not require local SSD caching.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is an x86_64 server featuring 56 vCPUs and 224.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 28 physical cores and dedicated CPU allocation. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show top 10% tier results in PassMark memory scores and small-model LLM text generation, alongside top 25% tier results in multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and database operations. Conversely, single-core processing, large-block memory bandwidth, and text processing benchmarks sit in the average tier. Supported by hardware-accelerated cryptography and vector extensions, this instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database workloads, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
